systems_shown: Back Office (software for managing orders, stores and customer groups)
metadata.main_topic: Implementing Audit History (change history) functionality in the Back Office

actions.result: the main interface with a sidebar and a table loads
actions.context: The tech lead switches to the Back Office tab. A left sidebar with navigation (Shops, Customer Groups, Orders) is visible, a top bar with multiple filter dropdowns, and a main work area filled by a large table of order data.

actions.result: a detailed product dashboard is shown
actions.context: Switch to the 'Demo Lamp' tab. The screen is a detailed dashboard with information panels (Description, Dimensions, Pricing, Stock, etc.).

actions.result: a modal window with a list of log entries opens
actions.context: In the top right corner of the screen, just above the 'Pricing' panel, the tech lead clicks a small button with a clock icon ('Product history').
A window with the change history opens. The rows contain a date, a user and text. The tech lead highlights specific texts with the mouse to explain how the log entries should look in plain language.

timeline.current_state: Modal window with the change history is open

actions.context: Back to the first tab with the orders list.

actions.result: a side panel (Sidebar) with details slides in
actions.context: Clicking a specific row in the large table. A side panel opens on the right, showing order details (Order, Status, Type, Date, User).

actions.result: a context menu/window for editing opens
actions.context: Clicking the blue 'Edit Item' button in the side panel, which opens a small update window.
Demonstration of a change: the 'Cancel' button is clicked to change the status of the order item.

actions.result: the status returns to its initial state (Pending)
actions.context: Immediately after that the 'Restore' button is clicked to return the order item to status 'Pending'.

timeline.current_state: The order details side panel is open

actions.element: + (Add) button next to Customer Groups in the sidebar
actions.result: the Create Customer Group modal window opens
actions.context: Clicking the plus icon next to 'Customer Groups' in the left sidebar. A centered modal window 'Create Customer Group' opens with fields for name and members.

actions.element: Order Type checkboxes (Retail, Wholesale, Retail & Wholesale)
actions.result: demonstration of the options that must be logged when changed
actions.context: Moving the cursor over the checkboxes at the bottom of the window ('Order Type') to illustrate that changing them must create a log entry.

timeline.current_state: The Create Customer Group modal window is open

actions.element: Add button next to Shops in the sidebar
actions.result: the Create Shop modal window opens
actions.context: Clicking the 'Add' button in the top section of the left sidebar ('Shops'). A small 'Create Shop' window opens with one text field and Cancel and Save buttons.

timeline.current_state: The Create Shop modal window is open, waiting for a name

actions.result: static screen, explanation of the backend logic (Doctrine, transactions)
actions.context: The screen stays static on the orders table. The modal windows are closed. The tech lead moves the cursor slightly without clicking while explaining the backend logic and Doctrine.

timeline.current_state: Static view of the orders table

actions.result: back to the modal window with the log entries
actions.context: Switching back to the 'reference-app' tab, where the window with the product history is still open.

actions.result: demonstration of where to place the new UI button
actions.context: The cursor is placed over the 'Extend all' text/button in the top right corner of the log table. The goal is to show visually where the new button must be built in the frontend.

timeline.current_state: Visualization of the desired final UI design
